شَجَرَةٌ مُجْتَثَّةٌ A tree [pulled up or out, by the root: or] that has no root in the ground. (A.) ―
-b2- بَحْرُ المُجْتَثِّ The fourteenth metre of verse; as though it were cut off from the خَفِيف; (TA;) the metre consisting of “مُسْتَفْعِلُنْ فَاعِلَاتُنْ فَاعِلَاتُنْ
” (K. [So originally; but in usage, the last of the three feet is cut off. Accord. to the TA, the first foot is properly written مُسْتَفْعِ لُنْ, as in some copies of the K.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
